title: Removal of More COVID-19 Restrictions and Its Impact on Hospitalisation Rates and Vaccine Programme
what_it_is: Removal of More COVID-19 Restrictions and Its Impact on Hospitalisation Rates and Vaccine Programme

sections.label: COVID-19 hospitalisation incidence rate
sections.summary: Hospitalisation incidence has fallen in the recent Omicron wave, but a manageable rate cannot be estimated because it depends on variant transmissibility and daily infections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As our society becomes more resilient to COVID-19 due to vaccinations as well as safe recovery from infections, we have observed that the incidence of hospitalisation has fallen in the most recent Omicron infection wave, compared to previous waves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: However, it is not possible to estimate a hospitalisation incidence rate which our healthcare capacity can handle, because it is also a function of the transmissibility of the variant and the number of people who get infected on a daily basis during a big wave.

sections.label: Moderna bivalent vaccine evaluation
sections.summary: The Health Sciences Authority has completed its evaluation of the Moderna bivalent vaccine and a decision will be announced soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) has completed the evaluation of the Moderna bivalent vaccine and a decision will be announced soon.

sections.label: MIS-C rates in young people
sections.summary: As of 29 August 2022, MIS-C incidence among infected under-18s was 5.7 per 100,000 for the fully vaccinated versus 38 per 100,000 for the not fully vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of 29 August 2022, amongst young people under the age of 18 who are infected with COVID-19, the incidence of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) was 5.7 per 100,000 for those fully vaccinated, versus 38 per 100,000 amongst those not fully vaccinated.

sections.label: COVID-19 vaccine safety and childhood schedule
sections.summary: There is no evidence of vaccine toxicity or developmental defects in children, and no plans to add COVID-19 vaccinations to the National Childhood Immunisation Schedule now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There is so far no evidence suggesting COVID-19 vaccines result in potential risk of toxicity to humans or developmental defects in children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There are no plans to include COVID-19 vaccinations into the National Childhood Immunisation Schedule at this point as the pandemic situation is dynamic and the recommendations continue to evolve with new data.

sections.label: Moderna vaccine for young children
sections.summary: HSA approved the two-dose Moderna vaccine for children aged six months to under five, with vaccinations timed around end-October or early November after examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: HSA has also approved the use of the Moderna vaccine, which is a two-dose vaccine, on children aged six months to under five years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But because cases are now low and we also want to vaccinate children below five and give the booster for children aged six to 12 years at the same location, it is more convenient for parents to bring siblings often falling into both age groups together to the vaccination centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But the older age groups, those in Primary schools, many of them are also getting into examination mode and given that the current situation is stable, the cases are relatively low, our intention, as we have announced at the MTF press conference, is to time it around end-October or early November, when examinations are over, so that, with peace of mind, parents can bring their children – those from six months up to 11 years old – either for their primary series or for their booster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As we open up vaccinations to all the children for booster or primary vaccination, we want to continue to disclose as much medical information as we can, for example, as the Member has asked, "What is the MIS-C rate for children who are fully vaccinated and not vaccinated?" We can tell there is huge difference.

sections.label: Review of vaccination-differentiated measures
sections.summary: The review of VDS together with vaccination requirements is ongoing and should be completed in the next couple of months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Nevertheless, as I mentioned in my main reply, we are reviewing VDS together with the requirements for vaccinations and it should be completed in the next couple of months.
